note: Feat desc: "Increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. This feat can't increase an ability score above 20." PickSchema's `abilities` variant can express only ONE `improve` grammar per choice (no either/or), and its enum has no '+1 to two abilities' shape at all (only '+1', '+2', '+2/+1', '+1/+1/+1') — so this picks the '+2' form, an exact match for the feat's first RAW option ("increase one ability score by 2"); the second RAW option ("+1 to two abilities") isn't expressible by any single choice under this schema and is dropped, per the same limitation noted on the background ability-score overlays. `at: {kind:'level', level:4}` records the earliest level either Fighter or Wizard can take this feat (both classes' `@4/feat` choice); 1b's choice-offering helpers (`derive/choices.ts`) don't yet walk a chosen feat's own `choices[]` the way they walk class/subclass level rows, so this sub-choice is reachable today only by `findChoice` resolving a decision recorded directly against its id — surfacing it as a requested/pending choice is Phase-4 scope. Since `repeatable: true` (R23), a character who takes this feat again at a later ASI level records a decision against this same choice id again; a per-instance choice id is also Phase-4 scope.
